summary.headline: Aditya Infotech Q2 FY27 revenue rose 89.9% YoY to INR 1,746 crore; EBITDA margin 17.6%, but FY27 EBITDA margin guided flat at 14-15% with H2 expected lower.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue was INR 1,746 crore (up 89.9% YoY, up 24.5% QoQ) with EBITDA of INR 307 crore at a 17.6% margin. PAT before exceptional item was INR 220 crore (up 214%); reported PAT was INR 185.5 crore after a INR 34.4 crore fire-related exceptional loss at the Kadapa plant, which is stated to be fully insured. Management raised FY27 revenue guidance to INR 6,500-6,800 crore and PAT margin guidance to 9-10%, while keeping EBITDA margin at 14-15% and saying H2 margins will be lower than Q2. The company completed a INR 1,500 crore QIP in September, repaid all borrowings in October and is now debt-free, and agreed to invest INR 45.4 crore for 30% of BLUE KGraph AI Solutions.

segments.name: CP PLUS (flagship brand)
segments.commentary: Contributed about 88% of Q2 revenue vs 86% a year ago; IP products are about 79% of the portfolio, up from 71%. Management says the company holds about 42% of total Indian video surveillance market (incl. unorganised) in the 12 months to Sept 2026, vs 30% at IPO.

segments.name: NEXIVUE
segments.commentary: Launched around April 2026 for entry and mid-market; management says initial pickup is good and first placements are happening, with expectation it becomes a leading brand after CP PLUS.

segments.name: EYRA
segments.commentary: Has not yet reached the market; first products expected to flow by end of November or December 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR 6,500-6,800 crore from INR 6,000-6,500 crore, implying 54-61% growth.

FY27 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 14-15% despite 16.3% in H1; management says H2 margins will be lower than Q2 as low-cost SOC and memory inventory is used up and price increases are moderated.
FY27 PAT margin guidance raised to 9-10% from 8.5-9.5%.
Capex of about INR 650 crore to roughly double capacity by late FY29 to early FY30 across Kadapa phase 3 and Greater Noida; capacity to start coming online in 18-24 months.
Backward integration benefits (housing/enclosures at Kadapa, cable JV) to accrue mainly in FY28; management has not modelled the margin benefit.
Management expects unit market CAGR of 18-20% over 3-5 years; value growth expected to exceed unit growth near term while input prices rise.
capex_capacity: Kadapa plant capacity is 2.5 million units per month; plan to more than double through Kadapa phase 3 (22 acres additional land acquired) and a new Greater Noida facility, funded from QIP.
Greater Noida: land acquired; civil construction to start in the next quarter. Planned fully integrated lens plant there with 2 million lenses per month.
Housing and enclosures plant at Kadapa begins trials this quarter with commercial production from next quarter; cable plant to go live in Q4 FY27.
Around INR 100 crore capex spent in H1 FY27 per analyst; management broadly cites about INR 650 crore total capex plan.
CP PLUS PRO premium enterprise range rollout planned for Q4 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management says the industry is moving toward cybersecurity-certified (STQC) products and trusted supply chains, which favours scaled domestic brands.
Price increases on SOC, DDR and flash were passed on gradually to the channel to avoid a sudden price shock; management says it is moderating price hikes to gain share.
H1 growth of about 90% was partly helped by a soft base last year, when STQC certification backlogs held back industry supply; growth will normalise in H2.

About 40-plus brands are STQC certified per the online portal, but management sees no significant on-ground traction from new entrants; no Chinese or land-border company is certified for any model, per management.
Distribution: 30,000-35,000 installers and resellers on the company app, plus about 2,000 installers and system integrators; management cites a 40-50% share bandwidth.
Management said the government policy for DVR/NVR STQC is still under work, with no notification yet; it would further benefit domestic brands once issued.
Management did not split the 90% growth between memory-led price, premiumisation and volume.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the implied H2 EBITDA margin of about 13% and how do backward integration benefits factor in?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said backward integration benefits will mainly start in FY28 once the housing plant and cable JV are online, and it is keeping 14-15% guidance as a cushion for market share strategy in a volatile input cost environment.

qa_highlights.question: What inorganic capabilities are being sought beyond BLUE?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to name targets; it described a 'CP PLUS 2.0' plan to move from hardware to solutions, cloud and AI, judged on capabilities, product adjacencies and geographic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any Chinese or other new competitor applying for STQC certification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is not aware of any such company certified for any model and that the government has strict trusted-supply-chain rules on land-border entities.

qa_highlights.question: Is there pushback on price hikes or demand impact that is causing the H2 price moderation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is keeping a cushion for competition, staggering pass-through of input costs, and aims for a competition-crushing share strategy; it did not report demand loss.

qa_highlights.question: Medium-term growth: value vs volume and margin upside from backward integration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 18-20% unit CAGR over 3-5 years; value growth should exceed unit growth near term. It agreed that localisation should lift margins above 14-15% in steady state but has not modelled the benefit.

qa_highlights.question: Capex plan and the housing plant spend?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 650 crore to double capacity by late FY29 to early FY30 across Kadapa phase 3 and Greater Noida; management did not have the specific housing plant spend and will follow up.

qa_highlights.question: Why did receivable days fall and is it structural?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it was a conscious effort to tighten collections linked to supply levels; it expects similar receivable levels across EYRA, NEXIVUE, CP PLUS and CP PLUS PRO on a blended basis.

risks_watch: H2 EBITDA margin likely below Q2's 17.6% as low-cost SOC and memory inventory is used up; the 14-15% full-year guidance implies H2 near 13%.
Working capital is elevated due to strategic SOC and memory stocking; inventory unwinding is needed for cash flow to improve.
Unresolved input cost trend for SOC, DDR and flash; management says the duration of price rises is unclear.
Growth normalisation in H2 after a soft STQC-backlog base last year.
Pending government policy on STQC for DVRs and NVRs from 1 April; timing and impact not yet defined.
Inorganic and export plans (18-24 months) are not detailed; BLUE is not expected to be a material revenue or EBITDA contributor in the near term.
EYRA is not yet launched; NEXIVUE's early uptake is still at first placements.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, market share and balance sheet, but cautious and deliberately conservative on H2 margins and on quantifying backward integration benefits. Management declined to give splits or numbers on several questions (growth mix, inorganic targets, export markets, BLUE revenue).
key_quotes: Q2 should not be read as the run rate.
As market leaders, we did not want to give the channel a sudden price shock and ensured that the momentum of overall market expansion as well as our market share growth continues.
We are not shifting away. It is more an add-on.
The cash flow is more a function of growth, Rahul.

Housing and enclosures plant at Kadapa (backward integration), trials this quarter, commercial production from next quarter

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided up to INR 6,500-6,800 crore (54-61% growth, midpoint ~54% shown as 54 is the low end; midpoint ~57.5%), backed by H1 revenue of INR 3,148 crore (+89.7%) and 43-45% market share target, while the ~INR 650 crore capex to double capacity only comes online over 18-24 months, so near-term backing is partial and largely demand/pricing driven.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin held at 14-15% despite 16.3% in H1 and 17.6% in Q2, implying H2 near 13% as low-cost SOC/memory inventory is used up and price hikes are moderated; backward integration benefits not modelled until FY28.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Housing/enclosures plant at Kadapa in trials now with commercial production next quarter, and cable plant live in Q4 FY27; the ~INR 650 crore Kadapa phase 3 and Greater Noida doubling only comes online over 18-24 months (late FY29 to early FY30).

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR 6,500-6,800 crore (54-61% growth) on H1 revenue of INR 3,148 crore (+89.7%) and 43-45% share target, though H2 growth is expected to normalise after a soft STQC-backlog base and the split between price, mix and volume was not disclosed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: About INR 650 crore capex to roughly double capacity by late FY29 to early FY30 is already committed, with Greater Noida land acquired, civil works starting next quarter and 22 acres added at Kadapa; QIP of INR 1,500 crore funded it.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management just raised FY27 revenue guidance to INR 6,500-6,800 crore and PAT margin to 9-10%, and kept EBITDA margin at 14-15% as a deliberate cushion despite 17.6% in Q2, so further upside is possible if H2 holds.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Input cost (SOC, DDR, flash) trend is unresolved and management says the duration of price rises is unclear; DVR/NVR STQC policy timing is unclear, and H2 growth normalises after a soft base.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: CP PLUS PRO premium enterprise range rollout is planned for Q4 FY27 and EYRA's first products are expected by end November or December 2026, while NEXIVUE is already in first placements (launched around April 2026).

rows.label: Debt-free balance sheet after QIP
rows.why: INR 1,500 crore QIP completed in September and all borrowings (INR 363 crore at 30 Sep) repaid in October, leaving cash of INR 1,434 crore at 30 Sep 2026.

rows.label: Receivable days and inventory unwind
rows.why: Receivable days fell to 87 from 93 in Q1 and 105 a year ago, but working capital stays elevated from SOC and memory stocking that must unwind for cash flow to improve.

rows.label: BLUE KGraph AI 30% stake and CP PLUS 2.0 inorganic push
rows.why: INR 45.4 crore for 30% of BLUE KGraph AI Solutions agreed, but BLUE is not expected to be a material revenue or EBITDA contributor near term and further targets were not named.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, 42% market share, FY27 revenue raise and the debt-free balance sheet, but deliberately cautious on H2 margins and on quantifying backward integration benefits; analysts pressed on the implied ~13% H2 margin, price moderation, and undisclosed growth splits and inor
